title: The Fourth, private
logline: White fireworks over the dock, from the shack steps, drawn for nobody. Gully, Maria, the kids grown, the pup. Wood's knee at the frame edge. Still not red.

panels.composition: The dock from the shack steps at night, white fireworks over blue: Gully, heavy now, pouring; Maria in the lawn chair; the daughter, thirteen, and the boy, ten, at the dock's end; the pup barking at the sky. At the page's bottom edge, a knee in worn jeans and a hand resting on it — Wood, on the steps, as much of him as the page allows. The fireworks white. Twenty-six years white.

characters.pose: thirteen and ten, at the dock's end
a knee and a hand at the bottom edge

image.prompt: a single full comic page with no panel borders, spare knowing ink line with economy, muted ochre and slate blue and sea-foam green washes, a dock at night seen from shack steps under white fireworks over a blue bay, a heavy older man pouring coffee, a woman in an old lawn chair, two children at the dock's end, a small three-legged dog barking at the sky, and at the bottom edge of the page a man's knee in worn jeans with a hand resting on it, no words

art.line: spare, knowing; economy of line; Era I's black spotting back on purpose in the mill run
art.palette: muted ochres, slate blues, misty sea-foam greens; luminous sunbreaks in the last spring
art.paper: Arches; bristol; the backs of motel registration cards

notes: Still white. A knee and a hand.
